chunk_findings.detail: When `full=False`, `status` is supposed to return the bounded MCP answer: the existing lists are cut by `_bound(data)` because `STATUS_LIST_LIMIT` exists to keep one tool result within the client limit. The new `by_tag` branch is added after `_bound` and inserts a `by_tag` view built from all `tasks` and `phases`. The documented view contains “per-value counts for every distinct tag in the KEY namespace,” and `BY_TAG_TOP_BLOCKERS` only caps blocker names inside each bucket, not the number of buckets. Given a repository with many distinct values for the requested key, e.g. `status(repo, full=False, by_tag="assignee")` with 10,000 distinct assignee tags, the returned `data["by_tag"]` contains 10,000 bucket objects and can exceed the single-tool-result limit that the bounded API path is supposed to avoid.

chunk_findings.detail: As the diff stands, the new `--by-tag` path never invokes `_by_tag_view`; the only added use of `by_tag` is `"by_tag_lines": _by_tag_lines(data["by_tag"]) if by_tag else []`. Nothing in the shown `status` body assigns `data["by_tag"]` (and if the view were added in the same `data.update({...})` literal, it still would not be visible via `data["by_tag"]` during evaluation). Therefore, calling `status` with a truthy `by_tag`—e.g. `ddflow status --by-tag wave`—hits the added line and raises `KeyError: 'by_tag'` before any per-wave counts are produced.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `by_tag` view is inserted into the returned `data` before `_bound`, but the call to `_by_tag_view` receives no `full` flag or bucket limit; the only new bound introduced is `BY_TAG_TOP_BLOCKERS`, which caps blockers *inside* each bucket, not the number of buckets. If a caller uses the MCP/bounded path (`full=False`) with a namespace that has many distinct values, e.g. 1000 tasks tagged `wave=1` through `wave=1000`, `status(repo, full=False, by_tag="wave")` can return 1000 bucket objects, contradicting the documented bounded answer and potentially exceeding the MCP client result limit. Conversely, if `_by_tag_view` self-limits without seeing `full`, then `full=True` will fail to “list everything” as documented.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/overview.py:259 (`status` / `by_tag`)

chunk_findings.detail: The `--by-tag` handler calls `_api().status(..., full=True, by_tag=by)` before checking `c.json`, so `ddflow status --by-tag KEY --json` uses the API’s full path. The surrounding truncation code in `overview.py` shows that `full` changes the slice used for list truncation (`full=True` keeps first+last rows, while the bounded path keeps the first `STATUS_LIST_LIMIT`). The MCP `call` lambda for the same command does not pass `full`. Thus, for a repo with more than `STATUS_LIST_LIMIT` rows in any list, the CLI JSON and the tool JSON for the same `by_tag` request return different sets of rows; agents using `--json` do not get the bounded tool payload.
